minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 7, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
MacLean at 5:02 p.m., on December 7, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 3, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury (arrived at 5:26 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1.  Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is Oso Viejo

City Council Minutes  1  December 7, 2009
   Neighbors Association v. City of Mission Viejo and City Council of the City of
  Mission Viejo, Case No. 00319861.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem MacLean recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Item CS1, he gave the Council an update but there
was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Mayor’s State of the City Address

  The City Council received Mayor Ury’s State of the City address.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Terisue George, M.V.: speaking to agenda item #19 which is being continued, she stated that she
opposes the AT&T/True Value cell tower and she will be back on January 4, 2010, to comment
further.

Ratinik Singh, M.V.: expressed opposition to the cell tower antenna proposal for agenda item
#19 and stated that he will return on January 4, 2010, to discuss his opposition in more detail.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: expressed concern about confusion with the February 2, 2010, special
election ballot and asked the City to explain the recall questions to the voters. She further asked
the City Attorney to start a full investigation into the allegations that recall signatures were
gathered by residents of another city.

Connie Lee, M.V.: stated that there has been a misunderstanding about the recall petitions and
that there is no need for someone to be a Mission Viejo resident to gather signatures; all you
really need is the voter to sign the petition and witness their own signature. Ms. Lee noted that
they had higher standards than that and the person who complained about the process is just
pulling a publicity stunt.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: read an email from a Lake Forest resident who reported that every day, for
at least part of the time, he was alone collecting recall signatures. She requested that every
single person who collected signatures be subpoenaed to get to the bottom of the illegal
signature-gathering activity.

City Council Minutes  2  December 7, 2009
 Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated Mission Viejo residents are witnessing the results of reckless
spending and he cited the Marguerite Tennis Center and the dog park as examples. Mr. Lenczyk
stated that the City can allow these expenditures but only at the users’ expense.

David Allen, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for supporting the 2009 Mission Viejo
Activities Committee Gift and Goodies Boutique and the Santa’s Arrival celebration. He stated
that the events are bigger, better and safer thanks to the City’s support.

Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: for the record, he announced that he was speaking as a resident of the
City (not as a Planning and Transportation Commissioner.) Mr. Sandzimier recounted his
experience with recall proponent Connie Lee during the signature gathering and stated that Ms.
Lee told him they were trying to gain control of the Council and Lance MacLean was the easiest
target.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4 and 7 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of November 16, 2009, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated November 6, 2009, in the amount of $856,241.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Fiscal Year 2008-09 Community Development Agency Annual Report

  Received, filed and directed staff to transmit the report to the State Controller.

City Council Minutes  3  December 7, 2009
 6.  Single Audit of Federally Assisted Grant Programs for the Fiscal Year Ended June
  30, 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  CAL-Card Procurement Program

  Approved full implementation of the CAL-Card Procurement Program.

9.  New Orleans Jazz/Dixie/Zydeco Concert Sponsorship

  Approved sponsoring a New Orleans Jazz/Dixie/Zydeco Concert conducted by Creative
  Arts Productions Foundation (CAP) at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior
  Center on March 14, 2010.

10.  Purchase of Fifteen 700 MHz Radios from the Public Safety Interoperable
  Communications Grant

  Authorized the City Manager to issue a purchase order to Motorola in the amount of
  $57,396.03 for the purchase of 700 MHz radio equipment.

11.  Contract to Provide Youth Programs

  Approved Amendment No.4 to the Contract Agreement with the Saddleback Valley
  Unified School District Department of Recreation and Community Services to provide
  Youth Recreation Programs in an amount of $700,000 per year for FY 2009-10 and FY
  2010-11.

12.  Interstate 5 Noise Barrier Scope Summary

  (1) Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-9-0505 between the Orange County
  Transportation Authority and the City of Mission Viejo for the Interstate 5 Noise Barrier
  Scope Summary; and (2) adopted Resolution 09-58 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-2010
  Budget to Establish Estimated Revenues and Appropriations for the Interstate 5 Noise
  Barrier Scope Summary.

13.  Citywide 2010 Pavement Management Program Update

  Awarded the contract in the amount of $57,250 to Nichols Consulting Engineers, Chtd.,
  for the subject project.

14.  CDBG-R Asphalt Overlays of Various Streets in the City of Mission Viejo 2009
  (CIP 838)

City Council Minutes  4  December 7, 2009
   Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $156,570 for subject project to All
  American Asphalt.

15.  Oso Creek Restoration and Protection Project-Environmental and Project
  Management Services (CIP 207)

  Awarded the contract in the amount of $75,885 to Dudek for environmental and project
  management services.

16.  Route to School Plan Improvements for De Portola Elementary School

  (1) Approved a new crossing guard at the north leg of the intersection of Spadra Lane and
  Preciados Drive; (2) directed staff to install a new striped crosswalk at the north leg of the
  intersection of Spadra Lane and Preciados Drive in conjunction with the installation of
  pedestrian school crossing signage and pavement striping for both directions; (3) directed
  staff to install a new striped crosswalk at the north leg of the intersection of Preciados
  Drive and Embajadores Lane in conjunction with a new stop sign for the southbound
  approach; and (4) directed staff to install a new striped crosswalk at the south leg of the
  intersection of Spadra Lane and Carranza Drive.

17.  Orange County Regional Recycling and Waste Diversion Grant Program

  Adopted Resolution 09-59 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-2010 Budget for the
  Integrated Waste Management Program for a Food Waste Composting Program.

18.  2009 and 2010 Closure and Holiday Dates for the Mission Viejo Library

  Approved the request to close the Library on December 24, 2009, as a holiday, and to
  close at 5:00 pm on December, 31, 2009, and as noted on Exhibit A (of the staff report)
  for calendar year 2010.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

19.  Appeal of Planned Development Permit PDP2009-215 and Minor Exception
  ME2009-97 filed by Gil Gonzalez of Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent for AT&T
  Wireless of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s September 28, 2009
  denial of a petition submitted by Jason Kozora of Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent
  for AT&T Mobility, to construct a wireless telecommunication facility at an existing
  True Value Hardware Store, Mission Viejo MarketPlace shopping center, 26006
  Marguerite Parkway, in the CC (Commercial Community) zone.

  At the request of the Appellant, this item was continued to the meeting of January 4,
  2010.

City Council Minutes  5  December 7, 2009
 OLD BUSINESS

20.  City Council Communication with Auditors

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Matt Lenton, Mayer Hoffman McCann P.C., Irvine: presented audit results, internal
  control communications and internal control recommendations.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed correspondence from Mayer Hoffman
  McCann P.C. (MHM), the City’s independent auditors, regarding the recently completed
  financial statement audit for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2009.

21.  Request for Proposals for Integrated Solid Waste Management Services

  Joe Sloan and Enrique Vazquez, Sloan Vazquez, LLC: presented answers to the questions
  that were presented at the last City Council Meeting.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  bifurcate the commercial and residential contracts by considering the temporary roll-off
  containers as part of the commercial contract and define commercial service as bin use
  only.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  move forward with a unified commercial and residential contract.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  define the term of the contract as 8 years with a two-year extension option.

City Council Minutes  6  December 7, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  Request for Proposals and the draft agreement for Integrated Solid Waste Management
  Services pursuant to the comments and decisions made during the discussion at this
  meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  During the discussion, the Council Members agreed that: (1) the weighting criteria will
  be included as proposed by the consultants; (2) new trucks will be required; (3) cart
  washing will be included in the RFP as an option; (4) the generic cart standard will be
  included with a note that this may be a negotiated item at a later date; and (5) the Code of
  Conduct will remain as presented.

22.  Appointment to Fill One Unscheduled Vacancy on the Community Services
  Commission and One Unscheduled Vacancy on the Investment Advisory
  Commission

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Schlicht,
  to appoint Tina Neukirch to the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  MacLean
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, Council Member
  Kelley nominated Dominic Nolan to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  7  December 7, 2009
 23.  Appointment to Fill One Unscheduled Vacancy on the Planning and Transportation
  Commission (Continued from the meeting of October 19, 2009)

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to appoint Barbara Anderson to the Planning
  and Transportation Commission. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Council Member Schlicht re-nominated Mark Dobrilovic to the Panning and
  Transportation Commission. Mayor Ury determined that the motion was out of order.

  Council Member Schlicht nominated Andre Hadzi-Pavlovic for the Planning and
  Transportation Commission.

  Because Mr. Hadzi-Pavlovic applied for the Investment Advisory Commission, Council
  Member stated that she would to seek a new application from him and return with her
  appointment at the meeting of January 4, 2010.

  Council Member Kelley noted that she has never seen so many excellent, well qualified,
  and interested candidates. She was struck by the professional backgrounds and with
  eighteen applications in front of us, she encouraged Council Member Schlicht to go back
  and read the applications, to be open-minded and to choose a candidate who will serve
  our City well.

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register dated November 13, 2009, in the amount of $630,155.47

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff to provide responses to questions she has heard
  from residents: (1) Check #00243090 – Outdoor Sign Systems Inc. – two Monument
  Signs for Crown Valley, $12,136.60; and (2) Check #00243122 – Tangram Interiors –
  one Chair for the Public Works Department - $737.33.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein indicated
  that staff will research the items and get back to the City Council with a response to these
  inquiries.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  December 7, 2009
   AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Shade Canopy Installation over the Bleachers at Various Sports Parks

  Mitch Hannah M.V.: encouraged the City Council to vote in favor of installing shade
  shelters at Mission Viejo sports parks.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
  construction specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

24.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

25.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that the next meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA
  will be held Thursday, December 10, 2009, therefore he has nothing to report.

26.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that the next meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA
  will be held Thursday, December 10, 2009, therefore he has nothing to report.

27.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg stated that earlier this evening Joyce Saltzgiver raised a question about
the recall ballot and staff has heard similar concerns from other residents. There seems to be

City Council Minutes  9  December 7, 2009
 question in the minds of the voters surrounding the fact that regardless of how one votes on the
recall, they still have an opportunity to vote for one of the candidates on the ballot. Given those
questions and with Council concurrence, Mr. Wilberg stated that he would like to have the City
Attorney work with the City Clerk to provide a bulletin to make sure to the voters of the
community know exactly what will be on the ballot and what they are allowed to vote on.

By consensus, the City Council agreed that the clarification would be a good idea.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

28.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Hawk Trot on November 20, 2009,
which was a fundraiser for the implementation of an International Baccalaureate Program (IB) at
Carl Hankey Elementary. The school spirit was outstanding and the event raised enough money
for the first eighteen months of the IB program. She stated that she hopes residents become
aware of this opportunity as they look at their options for schools. Council Member Kelley also
discussed her attendance at the tremendously successful Santa’s arrival celebration. She
announced that Santa will be in his workshop every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday through
December 20, 2009. The workshop is right here at the Civic Center, visits with Santa are free
and parents can bring their camera and take their own pictures. Council Member Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of December is caring. She
encouraged everyone to focus on the positive and remember the importance of kindness and
caring. Council Member Kelley concluded her comments by wishing residents a Merry
Christmas, Happy Hanukkah, and happy holidays.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma announced that he enjoyed the Santa’s arrival event and he observed
that the Civic Center location is far superior and much safer than prior locations. He expressed
his thanks to the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and the staff who make it all possible.
Council Member Ledesma wished everyone a Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukah and happy
holidays.

City Council Minutes  10  December 7, 2009
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that it is unconscionable if the City is engaged in trying to
disqualify the recall effort. Signing petitions is a constitutional right regardless of what we have
heard from one signature gatherer. She stated that she is curious to know how many petitions
that individual handed in and she noted that proponents did not submit those signatures. She
feels the process should go forward and she stated that there has been a lot of electioneering from
the dais over the past several months but the voters will make their decision on February 2, 2010.
Council Member Schlicht congratulated resident Connie Lee on her appointment as the Mission
Viejo GOP leader/captain and she noted that Ms. Lee also received special recognition a few
months ago for all the work she has done in the City, the County and the State. She also
congratulated the Mission Viejo Environmental Association on their new drought tolerant
display and she read the words from the display’s placard. She stated that the City should pull
up the grass and start using more native California plants. Council Member Schlicht stated that
it is sometimes brutal at the dais and although she’s not as smooth as some of her colleagues and
she suffers from stage fright, she does work hard for the City. She enjoys her position and she
appreciates the support and understanding she gets from the community. Finally, she wished
residents a Merry Christmas, Happy New Year and Happy Hanukkah to those who celebrate.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

29.  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean’s irrevocable rejection of available City Council Lifetime
  Retiree Health Insurance benefits; disclosure of written form of rejection;
  discussion of MPT MacLean’s City and Regional leadership activities

  By consensus, the City council received and accepted Mayor Pro Tem MacLean’s
  irrevocable voluntary rejection of Lifetime Retiree Health insurance benefit.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that he continues to be amazed with the barrage of innuendoes
and accusations from Council Member Schlicht. He has heard the words “irresponsible, corrupt,
abusive, and unconscionable electioneering.” He stated that she is the only one who brings up
the recall and who announces that she signed the petition. Just this evening, Council Member
Schlicht said that “this man needs to be removed from office.” Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated
that he is trying to take the high road yet he will respond to accusations as they are made. He
doesn’t introduce the subject of the recall or use his position to discuss it but he will not sit back
and continually be attacked with lies and innuendos without responding. He stated that anybody
at the dais should have the same opportunity without being accused of electioneering. Mayor
Pro Tem MacLean noted that he has responded in the past to some of the recall allegations and
pointed to documents and votes which completely refute the allegations and now he has seen an
email from Council Member Schlicht trying to find a way to prevent him from getting his

City Council Minutes  11  December 7, 2009
 message out. She is hoping to take away his first amendment rights and to tell his story. He
stated that Council Member Schlicht is the first one to try and take those rights away when it is
something that she doesn’t agree with. He noted that as he speaks, she is talking to the City
Attorney trying to figure out how to take the microphone away from him as he makes his
comments. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean encouraged everyone, particularly Council Member
Schlicht, to step the discussions up to the next level and to keep to the issues before the City and
take the personal shots out of it. He stated that he wants to talk about what’s good for this City
and move forward on the issues of importance and concern. He wants to get back to serving the
residents effectively and efficiently and take some of the personal angst and hatred out of it.
Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that he is here to serve the residents, not to publicly fight
with Council Member Schlicht. He concluded his comments by wishing his colleagues and the
residents a very Merry Christmas and Happy New Year. He looks forward to returning to
civilized discussions in the New Year and to following the Community of Character words of the
month.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury stated that he too had a great time at the Santa’s arrival celebration. So many people
come year after year and it is truly a wonderful event. He announced that he also attended the
fundraiser for the charter school proposal. It was an honor for him to be there and he is
impressed with the energy, effort and passion the residents have. Mayor Ury asked the City
Attorney if the City can send a letter in support of the charter school petition for the O’Neill site
and in response to the Superintendent’s denial of the petition.

City Attorney Curley confirmed that the City sent a previous letter in support of the charter
school proposal so a new letter can be sent as a follow-up.

Mayor Ury broke from his comments and asked Council Member Schlicht to sit down. He stated
that he is trying to finalize a meeting but because Council Member Schlicht has not gotten her
way, she is having an adult temper tantrum.

Continuing his comments, Mayor Ury stated that the work of the charter school supporters has a
lot of merit and there is a full plan for appealing the denial of the charter petition if it is shot
down at the Board Meeting. Ending his year as Mayor, he thanked staff for the proactive work
that they do and an overall excellent job. He thanked his colleagues for moving things forward
to try and make this City a better place and he expressed his appreciation, fondness and love to
his family for their support. Finally, Mayor Ury wished everyone a Merry Christmas, happy
holidays and Happy Hanukkah and he encouraged everyone to reflect on the wonderful City we
live in.

City Council Minutes  12  December 7, 2009
 CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

30.  Election of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tempore

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Mayor Ury, to appoint Trish
  Kelley as Mayor Pro Tem for the year 2010.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  appoint John Paul Ledesma as Mayor for 2010.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to appoint Lance
  MacLean as Mayor for 2010.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean and Ury
  NOES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:32 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, January 4, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 4, 2010

City Council Minutes  13  December 7, 2009
